main_text.head: PRÆFATIO.
main_text.p: Aug. de doct. Christ. lib. 2. cap. 16. & 18.Ut enim ad sacras Scripturas in-telligendas, conducit linguae Ho-braeae cognitio, ut ii optime nô-runt, qui eâ sunt imbuti; ità et eorum, ex iis nonnulli, qui ejus peritiam expertes fuerunt (nominatim Au-gustinus) agnoverunt. Ac multis sane nominibus ad hanc rem utilis est hujus linguae cognitio.

Primùm, ut rectiùs certiùsque de Interpretibus ac Commentatoribus judicium fieri possit. Ii enim variis sint, ac plurimùm saepe inter se differunt, unde fit, ut qui ipsum Hebraeum textum intueri nequit, de multorum locorum sensu fluctuare necesse habeat, nec quem sit Interpretem vel Commentatorem prae ceteris sequatur, intelligat. Ob hanc potissimum rationem, quae Interpretum diversitatem spectat, Hebraeae linguae pari ter ac Graecae cognitionem necessariam censuit Augustinus. Multa in hanc rem dici possent, multisque exemplis ostendere in promptu esset, quàm longè à S. Scriptorum mente aberrárunt viri alioqui eruditissimi.

page.notes: The title PRÆFATIO. is set in a large display face beneath an engraved vignette, which is described here and not transcribed. The opening word "Ut" sits in a woodcut initial; the initial letter is read as U (Ut), with doubt. The small note at top right, beside the vignette, is largely illegible and is not transcribed. Faint lines above the heading, and the left-margin fragments, look like show-through or the neighbouring page and are left out. The scan is very dark and blurred, so many words in the body are uncertain; the transcription follows the most likely readings and some words may be wrong, but no [?] was added to keep the text readable.
